items.followUp: Explain how temperature and pH affect the rate of enzyme action.

rubric.why: Identifies two important factors affecting enzyme action.
rubric.description: Names temperature and pH as factors affecting the rate.

rubric.why: Explains that enzymes have optimum conditions and can lose their working shape outside them.
rubric.description: Explains the effects of temperature and pH, including reduced activity or denaturation at unsuitable values.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining either factor.

rubric.why: Recognises another factor that changes the rate of enzyme action.
rubric.description: Names enzyme concentration, substrate concentration, or inhibitors as an additional factor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one additional factor.

modelAnswer: Temperature affects the rate of enzyme action; the rate rises up to the enzyme's optimum temperature.
Above the optimum temperature, the enzyme may denature and its activity decreases.
Each enzyme works best at a particular optimum pH; a different pH can reduce its activity or denature it.
Increasing enzyme concentration increases the rate when sufficient substrate is available.
Increasing substrate concentration increases the rate until all enzyme active sites are occupied; inhibitors can also reduce the rate.

items.followUp: Draw and label a simple diagram of an ATP molecule, showing its three main components.

rubric.why: Identifies the nitrogenous base and sugar in ATP.

rubric.description: States that ATP contains three phosphate groups.

rubric.why: Shows understanding of how ATP stores energy.
rubric.description: States that energy-rich bonds link the phosphate groups.

modelAnswer: ATP is a nucleotide made of the nitrogenous base adenine, a ribose sugar, and three phosphate groups.
Adenine is attached to ribose, and the ribose is attached to the chain of three phosphate groups.
The bonds between the phosphate groups are energy-rich; energy is released when the terminal phosphate is removed.

items.followUp: Describe three ways in which the liver helps maintain the body's internal conditions.

rubric.why: Recognises the liver's role in producing bile.
rubric.description: States that the liver produces bile, which helps emulsify fats.

rubric.why: Describes the liver's role in regulating blood glucose.
rubric.description: States that the liver converts excess glucose into glycogen and can convert glycogen back into glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct conversion; award the second mark for explaining blood-glucose regulation.

rubric.why: Identifies important liver functions in waste processing and protection from harmful substances.
rubric.description: Describes deamination and urea formation, or detoxification of harmful substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deamination/urea formation and 1 mark for detoxification.

modelAnswer: The liver produces bile, which emulsifies fats and helps their digestion.
It converts excess glucose into glycogen for storage and converts glycogen back into glucose when needed, helping regulate blood glucose.
It deaminates excess amino acids and converts the resulting ammonia into urea for excretion.
It detoxifies harmful substances, including alcohol and some drugs.
It stores vitamins and iron.

items.followUp: Briefly explain how forestry can be a career for a person with a biology background.

rubric.why: Identifies farming as a biology-related career.
rubric.description: States that biology can be applied in farming or agriculture.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant example of work or knowledge used in farming.
rubric.description: Mentions crop production, livestock care, animal husbandry, or another relevant farming application.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one suitable example.

modelAnswer: Farming is a career in which biological knowledge is used to grow crops and raise livestock.
Farmers apply biology to improve crop production, control pests and diseases, and care for animals.

items.followUp: What is one way data can be presented during data analysis, and what can scientists infer from it?

rubric.why: Explains that data analysis organises or presents collected information.
rubric.description: States that data are organised, tabulated, or shown in a graph.

rubric.why: Explains how analysis helps interpret results.
rubric.description: States that analysis helps draw conclusions, identify relationships, or support/reject a hypothesis.

modelAnswer: Data analysis organises and presents collected data, for example in tables or graphs.
It helps scientists identify patterns, draw conclusions, and decide whether the results support or reject the hypothesis.

items.followUp: Write two features that make a scientific hypothesis useful.

rubric.why: A scientific hypothesis must be capable of being checked.
rubric.description: States that a good hypothesis is testable by observation or experiment.

rubric.why: A good hypothesis should make a clear, useful prediction.
rubric.description: States that it is clear, specific, simple, or makes a prediction that can be investigated.

modelAnswer: A good hypothesis is clear and specific.
It is testable by observation or experiment and makes a prediction about the expected results.
